parts.text: (a) Fig. 9.1 shows a beam of α -particles moving towards a thin sheet of gold in a vacuum. Fig. 9.1 Detectors in the region surrounding the thin gold sheet detect the α -particles and determine the number of particles that travel in various directions. State and explain what can be deduced from the following observations.

ms.label: 9(a)(i)
ms.text:
mark both explanation and deduction together
nucleus is very small
very few α-particles hit or pass near to a nucleus

ms.label: 9(a)(ii)
ms.text:
mark both explanation and deduction together
nucleus is charged
(charged) α-particles experience a force

ms.label: 9(a)(iii)
ms.text:
mark both explanation and deduction together
centre / (small) part of atom OR nucleus includes most of the mass of the atom / is (very) dense
(α-particles move and) nucleus stays still

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) A beam that consists of both α -particles and β -particles is passed through a region of space where there is a magnetic field perpendicular to the direction of the beam. State two ways in which the deflection of the α -particles differs from that of the β -particles. 1. ............................................................................................................................................... 2. ............................................................................................................................................... [2]

ms.label: 9(b)
ms.text:
any two from:
opposite direction
